## Book Topics

- **The rule**: insure losses you can't absorb; cover small ones from your emergency fund (leave room for error)
- **Insurance words**: premium, deductible, claim, coverage limit, liability; premiums and deductibles move in opposite directions
- **Health insurance**: never go without; stay on a parent's plan until 26, get it through work, or use the marketplace; copay, coinsurance, and the out of pocket maximum (your worst case, capped at $10,600 in 2026); high deductible plans qualify for an HSA with a deductible of at least $1,700 and an out of pocket maximum of no more than $8,500
- **Auto insurance**: liability of at least 100/300/100; consider dropping collision and comprehensive on a cheap car
- **Renters insurance**: about $13 to $23 a month; choose replacement cost over actual cash value
- **Disability insurance**: about 1 in 4 of today's 20 year olds will become disabled before retirement age; take employer long term disability (about 60% of pay)
- **Life insurance**: only if someone depends on your income; buy term, about 10 times yearly income; skip whole life
- **Umbrella insurance**: $1 million or more of extra liability; revisit as net worth grows
- **What to skip**: extended warranties, phone insurance, life insurance with no dependents, single event policies

## Choosing a Deductible

A higher deductible lowers your premium but costs more on each claim. The break even point is how many years of premium savings it takes to cover the extra deductible.

**Formula:** Break even years = (Higher deductible − Lower deductible) ÷ Yearly premium savings

```{r}
#| label: deductible-bar-model
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Savings from a $1,000 deductible vs. a $500 deductible, year by year"
#| fig-asp: 0.50
library(ggplot2)
df_ded <- data.frame(
  year    = factor(paste0("Year ", 1:5), levels = paste0("Year ", 1:5)),
  savings = 150 * 1:5
)
df_ded$fill <- ifelse(df_ded$savings >= 500, "#48a56a", "#0e9aa7")
ggplot(df_ded, aes(x = year, y = savings, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "#1C1C1E", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 500, colour = "#f44242", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 550, label = "Extra $500 per claim",
           hjust = 0, colour = "#f44242", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("$", savings)), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 850), labels = function(x) paste0("$", x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Car insurance costs $1,500 a year with a $500 deductible, or $1,350 with a $1,000 deductible. ($1,000 − $500) ÷ $150 = about 3.3 years. If you file a claim less often than that, the higher deductible comes out ahead.

::: panel-tabset
## Excel

Put the higher deductible in `B2`, the lower deductible in `C2`, and the yearly savings in `D2`.

Break even years in `E2`:

```swift
=(B2-C2)/D2
```

Yearly gain if you file one claim every `F2` years:

```swift
=D2-(B2-C2)/F2
```

Copy row 2 down to compare several quotes.

## Python

```{python}
#| label: deductible-py
def break_even_years(high_deductible, low_deductible, yearly_savings):
    return (high_deductible - low_deductible) / yearly_savings

# $1,000 vs. $500 deductible, saving $150 a year
print(round(break_even_years(high_deductible=1000, low_deductible=500, yearly_savings=150), 2))

# other quotes you might see
quotes = [(1000, 500, 50), (1000, 500, 150), (1000, 500, 300), (2000, 500, 250), (2000, 1000, 120)]
for high, low, savings in quotes:
    print(f"${high:,} vs ${low:,}, save ${savings}/yr: {break_even_years(high, low, savings):.1f} years")

# expected yearly gain from the higher deductible if you file one claim every k years
for k in [2, 3, 5, 10]:
    print(f"claim every {k:>2} years: {150 - (1000 - 500) / k:+.0f} per year")
```

## R

```{r}
#| label: deductible-r
break_even_years <- function(high_deductible, low_deductible, yearly_savings) {
  (high_deductible - low_deductible) / yearly_savings
}

# $1,000 vs. $500 deductible, saving $150 a year
break_even_years(high_deductible = 1000, low_deductible = 500, yearly_savings = 150)

# other quotes you might see
quotes <- data.frame(
  high    = c(1000, 1000, 1000, 2000, 2000),
  low     = c(500, 500, 500, 500, 1000),
  savings = c(50, 150, 300, 250, 120)
)
quotes$break_even <- round(break_even_years(quotes$high, quotes$low, quotes$savings), 1)
quotes

# expected yearly gain from the higher deductible if you file one claim every k years
claim_every <- c(2, 3, 5, 10)
data.frame(
  claim_every_years = claim_every,
  yearly_gain       = 150 - (1000 - 500) / claim_every
)
```

A break even under one year means the higher deductible pays for itself almost at once. A break even of 10 years means the savings are too small to bother.

:::

How to read this result: a positive yearly gain means the higher deductible saves money on average. The gain turns negative only if you claim more often than the break even. Either way, pick the higher deductible only if your emergency fund can cover it.

## Comparing Two Health Plans

A health plan's real yearly cost is its premiums plus your share of medical bills, minus any money your employer puts in your HSA. Your share can never go above the out of pocket maximum.

**Formula:** Yearly cost = (Monthly premium × 12) + min(Medical bills, Out of pocket max) − Employer HSA money

This simple version assumes you pay all medical bills up to the out of pocket maximum, so it slightly overstates plans with coinsurance.

```{r}
#| label: health-bar-model
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Total yearly cost of two health plans in a healthy year and the worst year"
#| fig-asp: 0.55
library(ggplot2)
plan_cost <- function(monthly_premium, medical_cost, oop_max, employer_hsa) {
  monthly_premium * 12 + min(medical_cost, oop_max) - employer_hsa
}
df_hp <- data.frame(
  plan  = factor(rep(c("Plan A (low deductible)", "Plan B (high deductible + HSA)"), 2),
                 levels = c("Plan A (low deductible)", "Plan B (high deductible + HSA)")),
  year  = factor(rep(c("Healthy year", "Worst year"), each = 2),
                 levels = c("Healthy year", "Worst year")),
  cost  = c(plan_cost(100, 300, 3000, 0), plan_cost(40, 300, 5000, 500),
            plan_cost(100, Inf, 3000, 0), plan_cost(40, Inf, 5000, 500))
)
ggplot(df_hp, aes(x = year, y = cost, fill = plan)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65,
           colour = "#1C1C1E", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("$", formatC(cost, format = "d", big.mark = ","))),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Plan A (low deductible)" = "#0e9aa7",
                               "Plan B (high deductible + HSA)" = "#48a56a")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5600),
                     labels = function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")
```

Plan A has a $100 monthly premium and a $3,000 out of pocket maximum. Plan B has a $40 monthly premium, a $5,000 out of pocket maximum, and $500 a year from your employer in the HSA. In a healthy year ($300 of care), Plan A costs $1,500 and Plan B costs $280. In the worst year, Plan A costs $4,200 and Plan B costs $4,980.

::: panel-tabset
## Excel

Put the monthly premium in `B2`, medical bills in `C2`, the out of pocket maximum in `D2`, and employer HSA money in `E2`. Put Plan A in row 2 and Plan B in row 3.

Yearly cost in `F2` (copy to `F3`):

```swift
=B2*12+MIN(C2,D2)-E2
```

Cheaper plan for these medical bills:

```swift
=IF(F3<F2,"Plan B",IF(F3>F2,"Plan A","Tie"))
```

Change `C2:C3` together to test a healthy year, a bad year, or the worst year (use a large number like 999999).

## Python

```{python}
#| label: health-py
import polars as pl

def plan_cost(monthly_premium, medical_cost, oop_max, employer_hsa=0):
    return monthly_premium * 12 + min(medical_cost, oop_max) - employer_hsa

# Plan A vs. Plan B in a healthy year ($300 of care) and the worst year
print(pl.DataFrame({
    "year": ["healthy", "worst"],
    "plan_a": [plan_cost(100, c, oop_max=3000) for c in (300, float("inf"))],
    "plan_b": [plan_cost(40, c, oop_max=5000, employer_hsa=500) for c in (300, float("inf"))],
}))

# a range of medical years
bills = [0.0, 300.0, 1500.0, 3000.0, 4000.0, 4220.0, 4500.0, 5000.0, float("inf")]
tbl = pl.DataFrame({
    "medical_bills": bills,
    "plan_a": [plan_cost(100, b, oop_max=3000) for b in bills],
    "plan_b": [plan_cost(40, b, oop_max=5000, employer_hsa=500) for b in bills],
}).with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("plan_b") < pl.col("plan_a")).then(pl.lit("B"))
      .when(pl.col("plan_b") > pl.col("plan_a")).then(pl.lit("A"))
      .otherwise(pl.lit("tie")).alias("cheaper")
)
print(tbl)

# how many healthy years of Plan B savings cover one worst year?
print((4980 - 4200) / (1500 - 280))
```

## R

```{r}
#| label: health-r
plan_cost <- function(monthly_premium, medical_cost, oop_max, employer_hsa = 0) {
  monthly_premium * 12 + pmin(medical_cost, oop_max) - employer_hsa
}

# Plan A vs. Plan B in a healthy year ($300 of care) and the worst year
data.frame(
  year   = c("healthy", "worst"),
  plan_a = plan_cost(100, c(300, Inf), oop_max = 3000),
  plan_b = plan_cost(40, c(300, Inf), oop_max = 5000, employer_hsa = 500)
)

# a range of medical years
bills <- c(0, 300, 1500, 3000, 4000, 4220, 4500, 5000, Inf)
tbl <- data.frame(
  medical_bills = bills,
  plan_a        = plan_cost(100, bills, oop_max = 3000),
  plan_b        = plan_cost(40, bills, oop_max = 5000, employer_hsa = 500)
)
tbl$cheaper <- ifelse(tbl$plan_b < tbl$plan_a, "B",
                      ifelse(tbl$plan_b > tbl$plan_a, "A", "tie"))
tbl

# how many healthy years of Plan B savings cover one worst year?
(4980 - 4200) / (1500 - 280)
```

Plan B is cheaper in every year with less than $4,220 of medical bills. One healthy year of savings ($1,220) more than covers the $780 extra in a worst year.

:::

```{r}
#| label: health-cost-curve
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Yearly cost of each plan as medical bills grow"
#| fig-asp: 0.55
library(ggplot2)
plan_cost <- function(monthly_premium, medical_cost, oop_max, employer_hsa = 0) {
  monthly_premium * 12 + pmin(medical_cost, oop_max) - employer_hsa
}
bills <- seq(0, 7000, by = 50)
df_curve <- rbind(
  data.frame(bills = bills, cost = plan_cost(100, bills, 3000), plan = "Plan A (low deductible)"),
  data.frame(bills = bills, cost = plan_cost(40, bills, 5000, 500),
             plan = "Plan B (high deductible + HSA)")
)
ggplot(df_curve, aes(x = bills, y = cost, colour = plan)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4220, colour = "#f44242", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 4300, y = 1000, label = "Plans cost the same\nat $4,220 of bills",
           hjust = 0, colour = "#f44242", fontface = "bold", size = 3.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Plan A (low deductible)" = "#0e9aa7",
                                 "Plan B (high deductible + HSA)" = "#48a56a")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","))) +
  labs(x = "Medical bills in the year", y = "Total yearly cost", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

How to read this result: the gap between the lines is what you save (or lose) with Plan B. Below $4,220 of bills, Plan B wins by up to $1,220. Above it, Plan A wins by at most $780. If you put Plan B's savings into the HSA, one healthy year covers the difference.
